text:
In order to assess the change in air quality due to the proposed Airport Spur freeway this study will be concerned with two levels of analysis: macroscale and microscale.
The macroscale analysis will look at the effect the proposed highway project will have on total motor vehicle emissions in the proposed study area. It also estimates the expected emissions from aircraft operation at lengral Mitchell Field.
The microscale analysis will look at the pollutant concentrations for individual receptors located adjacent to the highway corridor.
To determine these impacts the Federal Highway Administration and the Environmental Protection Agency have proposed various techniques to evaluate the air quality in the vicinity of proposed nighway projects.
The air quality analysis presented is commensurate with existing state of the art techniques. A series of air quality manuals, based on research by the California Air Resources Board in cooperation with the Federal Highway Administration, has established acceptable methods for estimating pollutant concentration levels in the highway corridor. EPA's indirect source review guidelines entitled "Guidelines for Air Quality Maintenance Planning and Analysis, Volume 9: Evaluating Indirect Sources," outlines a procedure for estimating peak carbon monoxide (CO) concentrations with identified traffic data.
As a result of the analysis contained in this Air Quality Report, the air quality impact of the Airport Spur project, after construction will not violate the national standards.
In spite of projected increases in traffic, the control of vehicle emissions imposed on new vehicles will result in improving air quality conditions within the study area and Milwaukee County whether the project is built or not.
